### Version history

- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 11→12)** — the **worldgen batch**: deep **redstone ore** in the overworld and **fortresses** in the nether. Both write generated blocks, so the one stamp bumps 11→12 and — for the first time — discards **both** dimensions' block-diffs together on load (old worlds reboot from their seed with players kept; all eleven digests re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v18**: fortress chests are a new lazy-fill family on the **existing** `lootedChests` field (their index set is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectFortressSites`, mirroring the dungeon/shipwreck/treasure families — nothing new is stored), and the new blocks (`NetherBrick` 95, `RedstoneOre` 96, nether-brick slab/stairs 97–101) are appended `BlockId`s with additive item string ids. The retired redstone-dust recipe has no save impact (recipes aren't persisted).
- **v18** (dimensions — the nether) — adds optional top-level `worldgenVersion` and `dimensions`, and optional per-player `dimension`/`portalArrival` (all described above). `migrateSaveV17toV18` is a **pure version bump**: no data moves — the top-level world fields remain the overworld's, so every pre-v18 save loads as an overworld-only world with the guard grandfathered (no stamp ⇒ never fires). The nether's own generator (`lib/world/netherGeneration.ts`) is a separate byte contract with its own SHA-256 baselines; adding it changed **no overworld bytes**, so `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays **11** — but from here on a bump discards **both** dimensions' diffs together (one stamp governs the whole save). The `NetherPortal` `BlockId` (91) is appended and has no item; `Obsidian` (90) and the new items (buckets, flint & steel) are additive string ids.
- **v17** (the players array — multiplayer groundwork) — every per-player field moves off the top level into `players: SavedPlayer[]`; world-level fields (seed, worldType, difficulty, hardcore, changes, blockEntities, lootedChests, mobs, vehicles, dayClock, villagesSeeded) stay put. `SavedPlayer` keeps the old field names (one rename: the top-level `player` position becomes `position`) so the per-field validators are shared between migration and live restores. `migrateSaveV16toV17` is a pure field move wrapping a flat single-player save as `[{ id: "local", … }]`, and rewrites pet owners from the legacy literal `"player"` to `"local"` — `SavedMob.owner` is a real player id from here on. A single-player world always saves one `"local"` entry; a multiplayer server holds one entry per known account and restores a joining player's slice through the same `restorePlayerFields` mirror that `serialize()` writes. Hardcore's `gameOver` is per-player (`restoreGameOver(save, savedPlayer)` requires the world's `hardcore` flag as before).
- **Unreleased (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 10→11)** — **portable worldgen noise**. Every seed-determined noise call (terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, the underground speckle hash) moved from `Math.sin` — whose results are engine-defined, so the same seed could generate different terrain on different JS engines — to the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts`. Same formulas, near-identical terrain (all structural probes unchanged), but exact bytes shift: old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed, and all worldgen digests were re-baselined into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` per docs/testing.md. The save **schema stays v16** — no field changes. This makes seed + block-diff sync portable between a browser and a Bun multiplayer server, and is proven in CI by `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` (Chromium digest ≡ Bun baseline). Weather windows and the daylight curve moved to the same portable primitives (both transient/derived — no save impact).
- **0.12.0 (no save bump; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10)** — the **aquatic update**. Kelp/coral (`BlockId`s **appended**: 55–57), sunken **shipwrecks**, and **buried treasure** all write generated blocks, so the worldgen baseline bumps 9→10 (old worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed; the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md). The save **schema stays v16**: cod/salmon are fungible wild mobs (never persisted; `restoreMobs` in older builds drops unknown kinds), kelp growth/harvest rides the block diff, the `treasure_map`/`dried_kelp`/coral items are additive string ids with **no instance state** (the map's compass target is derived from the seed at runtime), and shipwreck/buried chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` index set unchanged (see above — the fill family is re-derived, not stored).
- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The new `faction`/`owner`/`sitting`/`targetId`/`retargetTimer` mob fields are session-side; only the durable ones land in `SavedMob`. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v9** (difficulty) — adds an optional top-level `difficulty` (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`). `migrateSaveV8toV9` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"normal"`, via `restoreDifficulty`). Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v8** (game modes) — adds an optional top-level `gameMode` (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`). `migrateSaveV7toV8` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"survival"`, via `restoreGameMode`). The mode is switchable in-game, so the _current_ mode is what's stored; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. No worldgen change — modes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
- **v5** (unchanged for fishing) — the active cast is the session-only `state.fishing` field (a transient bobber, like in-flight arrows and thrown spears); it is never serialized and is cleared on respawn. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12 → v13 → v14 → v15 → v16.
- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).

## Profiles & worlds

Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob. The two small manifests stay in localStorage (they are tiny and read synchronously during render) while the heavy blobs live in IndexedDB. Both manifests are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):

- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, localStorage) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`, localStorage) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldType, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`); `worldType` is the chosen generation preset (sanitized to `"default"` on read for unknown/legacy entries). Both are the source of truth for regeneration and are also written into the per-world `SaveData` blob.
- **`monecraft`/`worldSaves` (IndexedDB)** — one `SaveData` blob per world (the schema above), keyed by world id and read/written through `lib/game/saveStore.ts`. Legacy blobs under the localStorage `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` keys migrate in transparently (see below).

`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 12) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds. Since save v18 the stamp also lives **inside the `SaveData` blob** and the discard is actually **enforced** at engine boot (`applyWorldgenGuard` — it was documentation-only before); the `WorldMeta` copy remains for the world list.

**World types.** A world's `worldType` selects a generation preset (`lib/world/worldTypes.ts`). `generateWorld(world, worldType)` forks on it before any block write (`terrainConfigFor`, `lib/world/generation.ts`), varying only sea level and per-biome surface height; everything else reads `GEN`. The `"default"` branch returns the GEN values verbatim, so default worlds stay **byte-identical** to the pre-feature generator — the existing determinism hashes are unchanged. Each non-default type is its own deterministic save contract with its own SHA-256 baseline in `generation.test.ts`; `worldgenVersion` still guards all types (a deliberate change to any type's config bumps `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, discarding stale worlds of that vintage).

The game shell (`components/GameShell.tsx`) drives a profile-select → world-select → play state machine and remembers the tab's active world in `sessionStorage` so a reload resumes it (a fresh tab cold-starts at profile-select). Before a world mounts, its blob is preloaded by the shell's `WorldSaveGate` (IndexedDB reads are async; the engine boot in the mount callback stays synchronous) and handed down as a prop. Deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs (`deleteWorldsForProfile`). At mount the shell also requests `navigator.storage.persist()` — eviction protection — but only when at least one world exists, so a first-time visitor never sees Firefox's permission prompt.

### Legacy migration

`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). When a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists it creates a default "Player" profile (carrying the old global skin) and **copies** the save into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key — the copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original. A brand-new player with **no** legacy save gets nothing here; the menu opens straight into the create-profile form (`ProfileSelect` renders it whenever there are zero profiles), so their first act is naming and skinning a profile.

**localStorage → IndexedDB migration** follows the same copy-then-delete rule per world key: the shell mount sweeps every `minecraft_world_save_*` localStorage key (`worldSaves.migrateAll` — a prefix scan, so manifest-less `cloud:<id>` blobs and orphans are covered) and the store also migrates lazily on first read of a key. The localStorage original is removed only after the IndexedDB put durably commits; a failed copy leaves it authoritative (reads fall back to it), a corrupt blob is left in place, and the sweep is idempotent with no flag — an empty prefix scan is the terminal state.

## Autosave

Every 15s via `setInterval` (queued latest-wins write; the "Saved" toast fires on durable commit), plus an **unload flush** on `beforeunload`, `visibilitychange → hidden`, and `pagehide`. The flush starts the put synchronously on the warm connection and commits it explicitly (`IDBTransaction.commit()`); without the explicit commit, auto-commit waits for request callbacks a document mid-teardown never runs and the browser aborts the transaction. All three triggers matter: `beforeunload` fires before the navigation commits, so its transaction has the most teardown headroom (measured in headless Chromium, the later two alone lose the commit race on a large fraction of reloads — keeping `beforeunload` costs back/forward-cache eligibility in Firefox/Safari, a price worth paying for save durability), while `visibilitychange`/`pagehide` cover mobile app-switch and close, where `beforeunload` never fired reliably. "Save & Quit to Worlds" also persists before leaving, because the interval is cleared on unmount and no unload event fires on an in-app world switch; an immediate re-open reads through the store's write queue, so it can never see the pre-save state.

## Compatibility rules

- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Caveat: the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined — the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability.
- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
- Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

# Bun is pinned (not "latest") for reproducibility. Since worldgen v11 the pin
# is no longer load-bearing for the worldgen hash tests — seed-determined noise
# is bit-portable across JS engines (lib/world/noise.ts, proven by
# e2e/determinism.e2e.ts) — so a Bun bump should NOT shift those digests; if it
# ever does, that's a portability bug, not a re-baseline. See docs/testing.md.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun test
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

  e2e:
    # Browser e2e takes several times longer than verify, so it gates merges
    # to main (the push event), not every PR iteration — PRs still run the
    # full verify job, and renderer/input/shell work runs e2e locally per
    # AGENTS.md before landing.
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: bun run test:e2e
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

  # ── Deploy only after the whole gate is green (verify AND e2e), and only on a
  # push to main in THIS repo — the repository guard keeps forks and the
  # upstream repo (which sync this workflow but hold none of the deploy
  # secrets) from attempting a deploy and failing red on every push. A red CI
  # never ships. Platform on-push auto-deploys are OFF (Vercel via vercel.json
  # git.deploymentEnabled; Fly in its dashboard), so these jobs are the sole
  # deploy trigger. Each serializes across pushes on its own concurrency group
  # so overlapping merges release in order, not on top of each other. See
  # docs/deploy.md.
  deploy-web:
    needs: [verify, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5 # a hung deploy must not squat the (never-cancelled) slot
    permissions: {} # only curls an external hook — no repo-scoped token needed
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-web-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      # Fire the Vercel Deploy Hook. Hook-triggered builds stay Git-connected, so
      # VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA (the menu version badge) is still populated. -f
      # fails the job on a non-2xx; --max-time caps a hung request.
      - run: curl -fsS --max-time 30 -X POST "${{ secrets.VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL }}"

  deploy-server:
    needs: [verify, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20 # remote Fly build + rollout; bounds a hung deploy
    permissions:

      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@ed8efb33836e8b2096c7fd3ba1c8afe303ebbff1 # v1.6
      # The exact config the manual deploy uses — NEVER a bare `flyctl deploy`:
      # the repo root has no Dockerfile, so flyctl's scanner would ship the
      # Next.js web image to the game-server app and crash-loop it (deploy.md).
      # --remote-only builds on Fly's builders (no Docker daemon in the runner).
      - run: flyctl deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --remote-only
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …) working in this repository. This file is the single source of truth — CLAUDE.md imports it.

## Project

A Minecraft-inspired voxel game: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, Bun. Single-player, browser-based, client-only, saves to localStorage.

**Zero binary assets**: every asset is generated at runtime — textures and sprites from pixel code, sound and music synthesized via ZZFX/WebAudio. New content should follow this principle unless the user decides otherwise. The one sanctioned exception is the UI pixel font (Monocraft, a Minecraft-style face under the SIL OFL 1.1), self-hosted via `next/font/local` from the committed woff2 in `app/fonts/` — don't "fix" it back to a system font. `public/` holds only code (the service worker `sw.js`) — no images or media belong there.

## Commands

```bash
bun install        # Install dependencies
bun run dev        # Dev server at http://localhost:3000
bun run build      # Production build — part of the verification baseline
bun run lint       # ESLint (flat config, eslint .)
bun run typecheck  # next typegen + tsc --noEmit
bun run format     # Prettier --write (CI runs format:check — unformatted files fail the build)
bun test           # Unit + integration + component tests
bun run test:e2e   # Playwright browser smoke tests (needs `bunx playwright install chromium` once)
```

## Development Workflow

For a non-trivial change:

- **Branch only for big work.** A new feature, a large refactor or improvement, a dependency upgrade, or broad/risky work spanning many systems gets its own `<type>/<topic>` branch off `main` (e.g. `upgrade/next16-react19-three184`) so it lands as one reviewable unit. Minor work — bug fixes, small improvements, doc edits, single-purpose tweaks — commits straight to `main`, even when it touches a few files. Judge by scope and risk, not file count; when unsure, prefer `main`. Either way, the verify gate below must be green before anything lands on `main`.
- **Commit in focused slices.** One commit per logical slice (e.g. split a dead-code removal from the feature that replaces it). Keep `bun run lint` green at each commit so the branch stays bisectable. Use Conventional Commit messages; no `Co-Authored-By` trailers.
- **Explain the why in the commit body.** The subject says what changed; the body (separated by a blank line) explains why — the problem or motivation, and any non-obvious decision or trade-off. A body is required for anything beyond trivial edits (typos, formatting); `git log` should make sense without opening the PR.
- **Docs and tests ship _with_ the change — not later.** A change isn't done until the docs match it: the **Docs** section below says what each `docs/` file tracks, so update every page that covers what you touched — a `config.ts` tunable, a system, a mechanic, content, the save format — **not just the obviously behavioral ones** (a new tunable or a new test almost always has a companion doc that needs the same edit). Cover new logic with tests, keep the test coverage map current, and add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Flag any save-format or worldgen impact.
- **Verify before it lands** (before opening a PR, or before committing minor work straight to `main`): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, and `bun run build` green (the same list CI's `verify` job runs); `bun run test:e2e` for changes touching the renderer, input, or React shell. A manual gameplay pass is only needed for pointer-lock handling, touch-control handling (a real-device checklist — see docs/testing.md), or visual-appearance changes. Then confirm the docs, tests, and `CHANGELOG.md` cover everything you changed (see the docs bullet above) — that check is part of the gate, not an afterthought.
- **Open the PR against this fork's `main`** (`gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main`); do not add AI-attribution lines (e.g. "Generated with …") to the description. Pushing and opening PRs are user-authorized — don't push or open a PR unless asked.

## Docs

- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) — engine/renderer/audio/shell layers, step order, engine invariants & gotchas
- [docs/adding-content.md](docs/adding-content.md) — step-by-step: new block / item / recipe / mob / mechanic
- [docs/save-format.md](docs/save-format.md) — save schema, autosave, compatibility rules
- [docs/online.md](docs/online.md) — accounts/guests, cloud saves, invites, join tickets, env setup, local online dev
- [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) — first-time deploy runbook (Vercel + Neon + Fly.io), shared secrets, verify, troubleshooting
- [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md) — cutting a version: keep `package.json` ⇔ git tag ⇔ CHANGELOG heading in lockstep
- [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md) — the client↔game-server wire protocol (framing, handshake, tick contents, close codes, trust model)
- [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) — test coverage map and the worldgen hash re-baseline policy
- [docs/tuning.md](docs/tuning.md) — gameplay tunables in `config.ts`, grouped by effect with balance trade-offs
- [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md) — player guide (gameplay, survival, crafting, mobs, farming)
- [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md) — gameplay reference tables (recipes, blocks, mobs, items)
- `README.md` — player-facing controls and quick start

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun test
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

  e2e:
    # Browser e2e takes several times longer than verify, so it gates merges
    # to main (the push event), not every PR iteration — PRs still run the
    # full verify job, and renderer/input/shell work runs e2e locally per
    # AGENTS.md before landing.
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: bun run test:e2e
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

  # ── Deploy only after the whole gate is green (verify AND e2e), and only on a
  # push to main in THIS repo — the repository guard keeps forks and the
  # upstream repo (which sync this workflow but hold none of the deploy
  # secrets) from attempting a deploy and failing red on every push. A red CI
  # never ships. Platform on-push auto-deploys are OFF (Vercel via vercel.json
  # git.deploymentEnabled; Fly in its dashboard), so these jobs are the sole
  # deploy trigger. Each serializes across pushes on its own concurrency group
  # so overlapping merges release in order, not on top of each other. See
  # docs/deploy.md.
  deploy-web:
    needs: [verify, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5 # a hung deploy must not squat the (never-cancelled) slot
    permissions: {} # only curls an external hook — no repo-scoped token needed
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-web-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      # Fire the Vercel Deploy Hook. Hook-triggered builds stay Git-connected, so
      # VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA (the menu version badge) is still populated. -f
      # fails the job on a non-2xx; --max-time caps a hung request.
      - run: curl -fsS --max-time 30 -X POST "${{ secrets.VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL }}"

  deploy-server:
    needs: [verify, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20 # remote Fly build + rollout; bounds a hung deploy
    permissions:
      contents: read # checkout only; the deploy authenticates with FLY_API_TOKEN
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-server-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # so a mutable ref would be a supply-chain risk.
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@ed8efb33836e8b2096c7fd3ba1c8afe303ebbff1 # v1.6
      # The exact config the manual deploy uses — NEVER a bare `flyctl deploy`:
      # the repo root has no Dockerfile, so flyctl's scanner would ship the
      # Next.js web image to the game-server app and crash-loop it (deploy.md).
      # --remote-only builds on Fly's builders (no Docker daemon in the runner).
      - run: flyctl deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --remote-only

content.content:
AGENTS.md:7:A Minecraft-inspired voxel game: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, Bun. Single-player is browser-based and client-only, saving worlds to IndexedDB with no account needed. Online co-op adds accounts, cloud saves, and an authoritative Bun game server (`server/`) backed by Postgres — see [docs/online.md](docs/online.md) and [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md).
CONTRIBUTING.md:3:Monecraft is a Minecraft-inspired voxel game built with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, and Bun. It is single-player, browser-only, and saves to localStorage.
README.md:8:The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player is client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved in your browser (worlds in IndexedDB — room for big builds), no account needed. Or play **online co-op** (2–8 players): host a server-backed world with a free account and share an invite link — friends register and join in a click. See [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md#playing-online).
CHANGELOG.md:45:- **World saves move from localStorage to IndexedDB — big builds no longer risk the quota cliff**: a heavily-edited world's save is unbounded JSON, and localStorage's ~5–10 MB origin cap was the likeliest real data loss now that the PWA multiplies long-lived offline worlds ("Save failed" forever once over the line). Saves now live in an IndexedDB store (database `monecraft`) with far larger quotas; existing worlds migrate transparently on first launch (copy-then-delete per world — a mid-migration failure can never lose a blob), and the small profile/world manifests stay in localStorage. The unload save rides `beforeunload`/`visibilitychange`/`pagehide` with an explicitly committed transaction — mobile app-switch now flushes immediately (beforeunload never fired reliably there) instead of waiting for the next 15s autosave. The pause-menu "Saved" toast now means the write durably committed. Browsers without IndexedDB (some private modes) fall back to the old localStorage behavior wholesale; returning players also get a `navigator.storage.persist()` request for eviction protection. Save format itself is unchanged (still v17) — only the container moved; cloud saves and online worlds are untouched.
CHANGELOG.md:117:- **Portable worldgen noise** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` **10→11**, save schema stays v16): all seed-determined noise — terrain waves, biome fields, cave-walk trig, underground speckle/flora hashes, weather windows, the daylight curve — moved from engine-defined `Math.sin` to bit-portable implementations (`lib/world/noise.ts`), so the same seed now generates **byte-identical worlds on every JS engine**. This is the groundwork for online multiplayer (a Bun server and browser clients must agree on the generated baseline to sync worlds as seed + block diff) and retires the fragile "worldgen hashes are only valid on the pinned Bun" caveat. Terrain is visually unchanged (same formulas; every structural probe passed the re-baseline untouched), but exact bytes shift: **existing worlds reboot from their seed and discard block edits**, per the standard worldgen-bump policy. Digests re-baselined into the new `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`; a new Playwright spec (`e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`) proves Chromium/V8 regenerates the exact Bun/JSC baseline.
CHANGELOG.md:238:- **Multiple worlds & player profiles**: the game now opens to a menu instead of dropping straight into one fixed world. A **profile** (name + skin) owns a list of named **worlds**, like user accounts on a shared console — pick a profile, then pick or create a world to play. All client-side in localStorage; **zero new assets** (the menus reuse the existing Minecraft-style chrome and generated skin portraits)
CHANGELOG.md:330:  - Selection recolors the body live (material color swap, no rebuild) and persists as a player preference under its own localStorage key (`minecraft_skin_v1`), separate from the world save — it survives world resets. No save-format or worldgen impact
CHANGELOG.md:356:  - Pause-menu Sound section: master and music sliders plus mute, persisted under a separate localStorage key (`minecraft_audio_v1`)
CHANGELOG.md:395:- Quality tooling: `bun run typecheck` (tsc), Prettier + `.editorconfig`, GitHub Actions CI (lint, typecheck, format, test, build on pinned Bun)
docs/architecture.md:23:- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play (plus the `initialSave` blob preloaded by the shell's `WorldSaveGate` — IndexedDB reads are async, so the shell reads before mounting) and persists through the async world-save store (`lib/game/saveStore.ts`, IndexedDB `monecraft`/`worldSaves` keyed by world id). AGENTS.md:7:A Minecraft-inspired voxel game: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, Bun. CONTRIBUTING.md:3:Monecraft is a Minecraft-inspired voxel game built with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, and Bun. It is single-player, browser-only, and saves to localStorage.
README.md:8:The twist: **everything is procedural — zero binary assets.** Block textures and item sprites are painted from pixel code, all sound and music is synthesized at runtime, and lighting is computed per voxel. Single-player is client-only: keep **multiple worlds** under **multiple player profiles**, all saved in your browser (worlds in IndexedDB — room for big builds), no account needed. Or play **online co-op** (2–8 players): host a server-backed world with a free account and share an invite link — friends register and join in a click. See [docs/manual.md](docs/manual.md#playing-online).

# Contributing

Monecraft is a Minecraft-inspired voxel game built with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript (strict), Three.js, and Bun. It is single-player, browser-only, and saves to localStorage.

## Getting started

```bash
bun install
bun run dev     # http://localhost:3000
```

## Verification baseline

Every commit should keep all four of these green:

```bash
bun run lint        # ESLint (flat config)
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
bun test            # unit + integration + component tests
bun run build       # production build
bun run test:e2e    # Playwright browser smoke tests (run for renderer/input/shell changes)
```

`bun run format` applies Prettier; CI enforces `format:check` and runs the E2E suite. A manual gameplay pass is only needed for pointer-lock handling or visual-appearance changes — see `docs/testing.md`.

## Workflow

- **Branch** off `main` as `<type>/<topic>` (e.g. `feature/fishing`, `fix/mob-knockback`) for features and multi-file changes. Small doc-only or single-fix edits can go straight to `main`.
- **Commit in focused slices** — one logical change per commit, imperative messages (`Add block breaking crack overlay`), no Conventional-Commit prefixes, no attribution trailers. Keep every commit green so the branch stays bisectable.
- **Update docs in the same change.** When behavior or a documented concept changes, update `docs/` and add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

## Save compatibility (read before touching worldgen)

Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas. World generation must therefore produce **byte-identical** output for a given seed, and the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) must never change. The characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts` pin generator output with SHA-256 digests — if they fail after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash. See `docs/save-format.md` and `docs/testing.md`.

## Docs

- `docs/architecture.md` — layers, game loop order, engine invariants
- `docs/adding-content.md` — how to add a block / item / recipe / mob
- `docs/save-format.md` — save schema and compatibility rules
- `docs/testing.md` — what is tested and the hash re-baseline policy
- `docs/releasing.md` — cutting a version (keep `package.json`, the git tag, and the CHANGELOG heading in lockstep)

11	### Added
12	
13	- **Nether fortresses & deep redstone ore — the worldgen v12 batch (save v18 and protocol v4 unchanged; ⚠ existing worlds discard their block edits in BOTH dimensions and reboot from seed)**: the Nether gets a destination and redstone-lite gets its real ore, bundled into one `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump so players' edits are discarded once, not twice. **Fortresses** rise over the lava seas — an 11×11 nether-brick keep with four covered, railed bridges striding out to 7×7 watchtowers, glowstone lamps in the ceilings and windowed walls — holding the dimension's first **loot chests** (lazily filled on first open from their own table, riding the existing persisted `lootedChests` machinery: nether-brick salvage always, glowstone dust/gold/coal/bread/redstone dust often, and a rare tier of blazite ore, **obsidian** — a portal-repair kit — diamond ore, or a sapphire sword) and usually a **spawner** dripping imps and the odd scorcher under the same rules as dungeon spawners. Looting your first fortress chest unlocks the **Fortress Raider** advancement, with a **Fortress Chests Looted** statistic counting on. Placement is PRNG-pure (the carved nether has no seed-pure surface to validate against), which is what lets any engine — client, server shard, or replica — re-derive every chest and spawner cell from the seed alone; a separation floor guarantees two fortresses can never touch. The fortress material is yours to keep: **nether brick** smelts from netherrack 1:1 (no fuel) and crafts **slabs and stairs** at the family ratios — a second partial-block id range behind the same predicates, so auto step-up, mob grounding, and the floor-fitting refusal all just apply. Meanwhile the overworld's deeps (Y ≤ 24) now vein **redstone ore**: sliver-pickaxe-gated, each block shattering into 4–5 **redstone dust** plus Fortune's level — and the gold+coal dust recipe from redstone-lite's launch is **retired** (it was an explicit stopgap for exactly this batch; the recipe-book hint now reads "Mine redstone ore"). The ore pass runs last and replaces stone only, so it can neither shift another generation stream nor eat a dungeon's cobble walls; all eleven worldgen digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md, with every structural probe passing unchanged.
14	- **The Nether works in online worlds (protocol v3→v4; save format v18 and worldgen 11 unchanged)**: light a portal in a co-op world and step through, exactly like single-player — and the party can split, with some players in the overworld and some in the Nether at once. The player list tags anyone who's "· Nether", a toast announces each crossing, and travel is seamless on the same connection (no reconnect). Server side, a room now runs an authoritative engine **per active dimension** ("dimension shards"): the overworld always, the nether born lazily on the first travel (or a rejoin whose save slice says nether) and persisted + dropped after `NETHER_SHARD_LINGER_MS` (60 s, env-tunable) once empty — and because the per-voxel light cache turns out to be renderer-only, **headless server engines now skip the light bake entirely (~40 MB and a full-world BFS saved per engine)**, so a two-shard room costs about what a one-engine room did before and the 512 MB Fly VM sizing is unchanged. Everything dimension-scoped got a real seam: tick channels and mob keyframes fan out per dimension (a cross-dimension keyframe would mass-prune a replica's mobs), the melee lag-comp history ring is per-shard, every pose/cmd carries a required dimension stamp (the travel race guard — frames in flight across a swap are dropped, never force-pose-fought), persistence composes both world halves at the room level, the day clock mirrors from the overworld (sleep counts only overworld players), and the owner's Peaceful despawns hostiles in every shard. The client rebuilds its replica engine and renderer in place around the live socket when the server says `dim`, prunes/adopts other players' avatars as they cross (`playerDim`), and a reconnect that raced a travel adopts the new dimension before resyncing. Deliberate scope: mobs (pets included) and vehicles stay behind — they are dimension state (your wolf waits by the portal); a mounted player can't accrue portal dwell at all (a raft drifting through a frame must never travel — this also fixes single-player); in-Nether deaths still respawn in the Nether. A new two-browser e2e drives the whole journey — a host builds and ignites a frame with real networked block placements, travels, is followed, and comes home — and [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md) now carries the version-bump rollout runbook this deploy will follow.

content.content:
16	### Fixed
17	
18	- **A player who hasn't moved since joining an online world can now mine (voxel raycast degeneracy)**: the aim/mining raycast mishandled the case of an origin sitting exactly on a cell boundary with an axis-aligned look direction — exactly how the server seats every fresh joiner at spawn (integer coordinates). Two defects compounded in the DDA: a (negative-)zero direction component fell back to an epsilon whose sign could contradict the already-chosen step, and an on-boundary origin computed a zero first-crossing — so the ray stepped **sideways into a neighbor column at t=0 on an axis it never travels**. Digging "straight down" from a fresh seat therefore mined the _diagonal_ column — or nothing at all once that column was hollow (say, the host's earlier shaft) — until the player's first real movement produced fractional coordinates. Real players move immediately, which is why prod co-op never surfaced it; the flaky two-browser friend-dig e2e had been passing on server random-tick edits instead of the dig it claimed to test (its aim recipe now targets the block-underfoot center, and a new room-level regression pins a never-moved joiner's streamed `mineHeld` actually breaking the block). The fix — a zero component never steps its axis (`tMax = Infinity`) — applies to both copies of the traversal (`voxelRaycast` and `waterSurfaceRaycast`). Engine-only: no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change.
19	- **Online worlds now honor their stored game mode**: a "Creative mode" online world seated every first-time joiner in survival — the world's `gameMode` lived only in the web database, which the game server (memory persistence especially) never reads, so creative flight/palette/free-build silently never worked online. The join ticket now carries the world's mode (`gm` claim, minted by the web API which owns that row) and the room seats first-time joiners with it; a returning player's persisted slice still outranks the ticket, so an in-game mode switch survives rejoins.
20	- **Arriving in a portal can never bounce you back through it**: two belt-and-braces latches keep an idle traveler where they landed. A player who _appears_ inside a portal surface — a rejoin after leaving latched, a travel handoff — now boots latched (only walking in travels), and the online replica pauses its pose stream during the brief travel-swap window (the fresh replica seats `self` at a generic spawn until the worldSync corrects it; streaming that transient position could walk the server-side player out of the arrival portal, clear the latch, and send them ping-ponging between dimensions every few seconds).
21	- **A bed respawn point is now honored only in its own dimension**: the spawn point stored bare block coordinates, and the same coordinates index a different voxel in each world — so dying in the Nether could false-positive on whatever happened to occupy the overworld bed's cell there. Bed spawn points now carry a dimension stamp (optional save field, additive — old saves read as overworld); respawn falls through to a safe local spot when the bed belongs to the other world.
22	- **Deflaked the simulated-latency FIFO (a real reorder, not a test artifact)**: the latency-simulation knob scheduled one `setTimeout` per delayed message, relying on the timer heap to fire equal-deadline timers in creation order — but that tie-breaking is not stable in Bun, and the monotonic delivery cursor _clamps_ every message behind a high jitter draw to the exact same deadline, making ties the common case. Result: rare genuine reordering of simulated-latency traffic (caught by the jitter-FIFO unit test going red on `main`, ~2/100 locally). Each direction now drains through a queued **delay line** — the same cursor, but one timer chain delivering in queue order, so FIFO comes from the queue rather than from timer tie-breaking; `dispose()` clears both lines, so no stray delivery timers outlive a session. Dev/testing code path only (simulated latency is never on in real play) — no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change — though the lagged multiplayer e2e steps (400±100 ms) inherit the stronger ordering guarantee.
23	- **CI: forks no longer attempt (and fail) prod deploys**: the `deploy-web` / `deploy-server` jobs now carry a `github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'` guard. The upstream repo syncs this workflow but holds none of the deploy secrets, so every push to its `main` went red on `curl -X POST ""` / an unauthenticated `flyctl deploy` — nothing ever deployed (secrets are repo-scoped), it was pure noise. Outside this repo the jobs now skip instead of fail.
24	- **Deflaked the worldgen-determinism e2e**: the spec paused the engine from its test body, but the game had already been simulating live through the whole boot window (menus → first rendered frames) — and a fresh seed-1337 world is _not_ free of random-tickable blocks (worldgen leaves ~31 cave-exposed dirt columns beside grass and ~23 growable kelp stalks within random-tick range of spawn), so on a slow CI runner a `Math.random` grass-spread or kelp-growth roll could land one block edit before the hash and trip the `changes.length === 0` guard (the digest itself was never wrong — the guard fired exactly as designed). The `gamePage` fixture gains a `pauseOnBoot` option that traps the `window.__monecraft` assignment and pauses synchronously **before the engine's first step**, so the hashed bytes are provably untouched by simulation; the determinism spec opts in. Test-only — no product code, save-format, worldgen, or protocol change.

- **Online worlds now honor their stored game mode**: a "Creative mode" online world seated every first-time joiner in survival — the world's `gameMode` lived only in the web database, which the game server (memory persistence especially) never reads, so creative flight/palette/free-build silently never worked online. The join ticket now carries the world's mode (`gm` claim, minted by the web API which owns that row) and the room seats first-time joiners with it; a returning player's persisted slice still outranks the ticket, so an in-game mode switch survives rejoins.
- **Arriving in a portal can never bounce you back through it**: two belt-and-braces latches keep an idle traveler where they landed. A player who _appears_ inside a portal surface — a rejoin after leaving latched, a travel handoff — now boots latched (only walking in travels), and the online replica pauses its pose stream during the brief travel-swap window (the fresh replica seats `self` at a generic spawn until the worldSync corrects it; streaming that transient position could walk the server-side player out of the arrival portal, clear the latch, and send them ping-ponging between dimensions every few seconds).
- **A bed respawn point is now honored only in its own dimension**: the spawn point stored bare block coordinates, and the same coordinates index a different voxel in each world — so dying in the Nether could false-positive on whatever happened to occupy the overworld bed's cell there. Bed spawn points now carry a dimension stamp (optional save field, additive — old saves read as overworld); respawn falls through to a safe local spot when the bed belongs to the other world.
- **Deflaked the simulated-latency FIFO (a real reorder, not a test artifact)**: the latency-simulation knob scheduled one `setTimeout` per delayed message, relying on the timer heap to fire equal-deadline timers in creation order — but that tie-breaking is not stable in Bun, and the monotonic delivery cursor _clamps_ every message behind a high jitter draw to the exact same deadline, making ties the common case. Result: rare genuine reordering of simulated-latency traffic (caught by the jitter-FIFO unit test going red on `main`, ~2/100 locally). Each direction now drains through a queued **delay line** — the same cursor, but one timer chain delivering in queue order, so FIFO comes from the queue rather than from timer tie-breaking; `dispose()` clears both lines, so no stray delivery timers outlive a session. Dev/testing code path only (simulated latency is never on in real play) — no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change — though the lagged multiplayer e2e steps (400±100 ms) inherit the stronger ordering guarantee.
- **CI: forks no longer attempt (and fail) prod deploys**: the `deploy-web` / `deploy-server` jobs now carry a `github.repository == 'hutusi/monecraft'` guard. The upstream repo syncs this workflow but holds none of the deploy secrets, so every push to its `main` went red on `curl -X POST ""` / an unauthenticated `flyctl deploy` — nothing ever deployed (secrets are repo-scoped), it was pure noise. Outside this repo the jobs now skip instead of fail.
- **Deflaked the worldgen-determinism e2e**: the spec paused the engine from its test body, but the game had already been simulating live through the whole boot window (menus → first rendered frames) — and a fresh seed-1337 world is _not_ free of random-tickable blocks (worldgen leaves ~31 cave-exposed dirt columns beside grass and ~23 growable kelp stalks within random-tick range of spawn), so on a slow CI runner a `Math.random` grass-spread or kelp-growth roll could land one block edit before the hash and trip the `changes.length === 0` guard (the digest itself was never wrong — the guard fired exactly as designed). The `gamePage` fixture gains a `pauseOnBoot` option that traps the `window.__monecraft` assignment and pauses synchronously **before the engine's first step**, so the hashed bytes are provably untouched by simulation; the determinism spec opts in. Test-only — no product code, save-format, worldgen, or protocol change.

content.text:
Latest is **1.3.14** — exactly what you already run locally. That changes my answer.

You're right, and my plan was wrong here. Pinning at 1.3.12 would enshrine a version *nobody* runs: CI and the Fly server would sit two patches behind the only machine anyone actually develops on, and your next `bun install` would still drift from the pin. That's documenting the drift rather than fixing it — half a fix.

One nuance I'd hold onto: pin **exactly 1.3.14**, not `latest`. A moving target defeats the point of a pin.

The one thing that makes me want to verify rather than just do it: this bumps the **prod game server's runtime** (`oven/bun:1.3.14` on Fly), and this branch already carries a migration and a synchronized deploy. And the repo makes a specific falsifiable claim — `ci.yml`, `Dockerfile`, and `testing.md:110` all say a Bun bump should *not* shift the worldgen digests, because the noise is engine-portable since v11. That claim has never actually been tested by a bump. This one tests it.

So: I'll pin 1.3.14 and run the digest tests. If a digest moves, that's a portability bug per the repo's own policy — I'd stop and report it, **not** re-baseline.

- **A player who hasn't moved since joining an online world can now mine (voxel raycast degeneracy)**: the aim/mining raycast mishandled the case of an origin sitting exactly on a cell boundary with an axis-aligned look direction — exactly how the server seats every fresh joiner at spawn (integer coordinates). Two defects compounded in the DDA: a (negative-)zero direction component fell back to an epsilon whose sign could contradict the already-chosen step, and an on-boundary origin computed a zero first-crossing — so the ray stepped **sideways into a neighbor column at t=0 on an axis it never travels**. Digging "straight down" from a fresh seat therefore mined the _diagonal_ column — or nothing at all once that column was hollow (say, the host's earlier shaft) — until the player's first real movement produced fractional coordinates. Real players move immediately, which is why prod co-op never surfaced it; the flaky two-browser friend-dig e2e had been passing on server random-tick edits instead of the dig it claimed to test (its aim recipe now targets the block-underfoot center, and a new room-level regression pins a never-moved joiner's streamed `mineHeld` actually breaking the block). The fix — a zero component never steps its axis (`tMax = Infinity`) — applies to both copies of the traversal (`voxelRaycast` and `waterSurfaceRaycast`). Engine-only: no save-format, worldgen, or protocol change.

- **Online worlds now honor their stored game mode**: a "Creative mode" online world seated every first-time joiner in survival — the world's `gameMode` lived only in the web database, which the game server (memory persistence especially) never reads, so creative flight/palette/free-build silently never worked online. The join ticket now carries the world's mode (`gm` claim, minted by the web API which owns that row) and the room seats first-time joiners with it; a returning player's persisted slice still outranks the ticket, so an in-game mode switch survives rejoins.

- **Arriving in a portal can never bounce you back through it**: two belt-and-braces latches keep an idle traveler where they landed. A player who _appears_ inside a portal surface — a rejoin after leaving latched, a travel handoff — now boots latched (only walking in travels), and the online replica pauses its pose stream during the brief travel-swap window (the fresh replica seats `self` at a generic spawn until the worldSync corrects it; streaming that transient position could walk the server-side player out of the arrival portal, clear the latch, and send them ping-ponging between dimensions every few seconds).

content.text:
Two things worth reporting before I write this.

**Good news:** the `kind` gate closes the server-side bomb vector entirely. `parseSaveBlob` is only reachable via `loadWorld` ← `roomRegistry.ts:41`, and rooms only exist for `mp` worlds (`mintTicket` rejects non-mp). So once members can't PUT mp blobs, the game server only ever gunzips blobs it wrote itself. The bound is still worth adding at that trust boundary, but it's defense-in-depth — not the live DoS codex described. I'll say so rather than overclaim.

**Less good:** I found the premise of your PUT-gate answer is shakier than I presented it. I told you sp-cloud worlds are single-owner in practice, so owner-gating PUT would be belt-and-braces. But `createInvite` (`worldsService.ts:280`) has **no kind check** — an owner can mint an invite for an *sp-cloud* world via the API. That member then can't even play it (`mintTicket` needs `kind === "mp"`), but they *can* read and overwrite its save blob, which my gate would still permit.

The cleanest fix isn't to revisit the PUT gate — it's that invites are an `mp` concept and `createInvite` should say so. That kills the "sp-cloud member" class at its source. I'll add it to commit 11 where the invite logic lives. It needs the owner to deliberately hand-roll an API call against their own world, so it's low severity — but say the word if you'd rather I owner-gate PUT as well.

Writing commit 2 now.

syncing and warns (rather than clobber the other device), then adopts the
newer save on the next open.

`worlds.saveBlob` column, but they do not share its ownership: an `sp-cloud`
blob **is** the client's upload, while an `mp` blob is the game server's
authoritative persistence (`server/persistence.ts`), which a room reloads as
world state on its next boot. So `putSaveBlob` gates on `kind` — otherwise
membership alone would let an invited player hand the room whatever world they
liked, bypassing the server authority [protocol.md](protocol.md#trust-model)
reserves ("clients cannot invent items or edits"). Nothing legitimate uploads an
`mp` world: `useMinecraftGame`'s push returns early when online, and mp worlds
carry no `cloudId`. `mintTicket` makes the mirror-image check (`mp` only), so
the two save paths stay disjoint. Reads stay membership-gated for both — a
member can already see the world by playing it.

Stored blobs are inflated through a bounded gunzip
(`MAX_DECOMPRESSED_SAVE_BYTES`, `server/persistence.ts`): gzip ratios run
~1000:1 on hostile input, so an unbounded inflate would turn a few MiB of
stored bytes into GiB of heap on the 512 MB VM. With the kind gate above, a
room should only ever read blobs the server itself wrote, so this is depth
rather than a live vector — but it is the seam where stored bytes become engine
state, and it shouldn't trust the row on the far side.

input.new_string:
### Fixed

- **An invited player can no longer overwrite a multiplayer world's authoritative save**: `sp-cloud` and `mp` worlds keep their save in the same `worlds.saveBlob` column, but they don't share its ownership — an `sp-cloud` blob **is** the client's upload, while an `mp` blob is the game server's authoritative persistence, which a room reloads as world state on its next boot. `PUT /api/worlds/:id/save` gated on membership but never on `kind`, so anyone holding an invite could upload a crafted `SaveData` over a shared world and have the server adopt it wholesale on the next room boot — inventories, builds, the lot — bypassing the server authority the protocol reserves for itself ("clients cannot invent items or edits", [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md#trust-model)). Nothing legitimate ever uploaded an `mp` world (the in-game push returns early when online, and mp worlds carry no `cloudId`), so uploads are now `sp-cloud`-only — the mirror image of the `mp`-only check the join-ticket path already made. Reads stay membership-gated: a member can already see the world by playing it. Separately, the upload route now rejects an oversized body on its declared `content-length` before buffering it, and stored blobs inflate through a bounded gunzip (gzip runs ~1000:1 on hostile input, so an unbounded inflate turns a few MiB of stored bytes into GiB of heap on a 512 MB VM) — with the kind gate in place a room should only ever read blobs it wrote itself, so that bound is defense in depth rather than a live vector, but it's the seam where stored bytes become engine state and shouldn't trust the row on the far side.
- **Docs: corrected stale "client-only / localStorage / `Math.sin`" claims**:

putSaveBlob gated on membership but never on kind. So anyone holding an
invite to a shared world could PUT a crafted SaveData over it and have
the server adopt it wholesale on the next boot — inventories, builds,
the lot. That is precisely the authority docs/protocol.md reserves for
the server ("clients cannot invent items or edits"); the trust model
concedes exactly one soft spot (a claimed eye pose) and this was not it.

Nothing legitimate uploads an mp world: useMinecraftGame's push returns
early when online, and mp worlds carry no cloudId. So uploads are now
sp-cloud-only, mirroring the mp-only check mintTicket already makes in
the other direction — the two save paths are disjoint and now say so.
Reads stay membership-gated, per the module's stated contract: a member
can already see the world by playing it.

Also bound what a blob can cost us:

- The route rejected an oversized body only after buffering the whole
  thing. It now checks the declared content-length first, keeping the
  post-read check as the enforcement (a missing or lying header still
  hits it).
- parseSaveBlob inflated without limit. Gzip runs ~1000:1 on hostile
  input, so a few MiB of stored bytes becomes GiB of heap on a 512 MB
  VM. It now streams through a running cap and cancels on breach, so the
  bound is on what is ALLOCATED, not on what is returned. With the kind
  gate above, a room should only ever read blobs the server itself
  wrote, so this is depth rather than a live vector — but it is the seam
  where stored bytes become engine state and should not trust the row on
  the far side of it.

The bomb regression test deliberately uses a valid, parseable save
inflated past the cap rather than garbage: garbage proves nothing, since
an unbounded inflate would allocate it all and still return null from
the JSON parse. Verified the test fails against the old unbounded code.

The `mp` gate leaves one narrow path open, closed separately: createInvite
has no kind check, so an owner can hand-roll an invite to an sp-cloud
world and that member may then write its blob.

**Two of eleven commits are in.** Where things stand:

**Commit 1 — docs + Bun pin (`148e9fd`).** Pinned at 1.3.14 per your call, from a single `.bun-version` that CI reads via `bun-version-file`. The bump turned out to be worth more than a tidy-up: the repo claims in three places that a Bun bump can't shift the worldgen digests, and that claim had never actually been tested by one. It holds — all eleven digests green, full suite 1497 pass, typecheck and build green. I also found three stale docs codex missed, including `manual.md` telling *players* their saves live in localStorage, contradicting its own line 33.

**Commit 2 — save endpoint (`85bf73f`).** The `kind` gate, the `content-length` pre-check, and a bounded gunzip. Two things I'd flag:

The **decompression bomb is less severe than reported**. `parseSaveBlob` is only reachable from `roomRegistry`, and rooms only exist for `mp` worlds — so once members can't PUT mp blobs, the server only ever gunzips its own output. I kept the bound as defense-in-depth and said so in the commit rather than claiming a fix for a live DoS.

The **bomb test needed rewriting before it was worth anything**. My first version used 8 MiB of zeros, which the *old* unbounded code also rejects — via the JSON parse, after inflating all 8 MiB. It would have passed with or without the fix. I checked by running the old implementation against it, then rewrote it to use a valid parseable save inflated past the cap, where only the cap can produce the null.

One thing needing your eventual call, not urgent: `createInvite` has no `kind` check, so an owner can hand-roll an invite to an `sp-cloud` world, and that member can then write its blob — my gate permits sp-cloud writes from any member. Low severity (needs a deliberate raw API call against your own world, and the UI never offers it), and I'm closing it in commit 11 by making invites `mp`-only. Flagging because it does undercut the "sp-cloud worlds are single-owner in practice" reasoning behind your earlier PUT-gate answer.

content.content:
110	## Compatibility rules
111	
112	- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
113	- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Since worldgen v11 the digests are **engine-portable**, not Bun-specific: every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable primitives in `lib/world/noise.ts` (see the v11 entry above), and `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves a Chromium digest matches the Bun baseline. So these tests do cover cross-browser save portability — and a Bun bump that shifts a digest is a portability bug to fix, not a re-baseline.

## Compatibility rules

- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Since worldgen v11 the digests are **engine-portable**, not Bun-specific: every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable primitives in `lib/world/noise.ts` (see the v11 entry above), and `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves a Chromium digest matches the Bun baseline. So these tests do cover cross-browser save portability — and a Bun bump that shifts a digest is a portability bug to fix, not a re-baseline.
- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
- Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

input.new_string:
- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
- **`parseSave` is the one seam that guarantees shape; the engine trusts it.** Every reader — `readSave` (legacy localStorage + the server's load path), the IndexedDB store, and the cloud download — goes through it, and nothing downstream re-checks structure: the engine's constructor does `save.players.find((p) => p.id === …)` and `applySavedChanges` destructures each change as a tuple, so a null player or a non-iterable change throws _there_ if it gets that far. `parseSave` therefore validates **entries**, not just the container types: player entries must be objects carrying a string `id`, changes must be `[index, blockId]` pairs of non-negative integers with the block inside the voxel array's `0–255` storage width, and a `dimensions` section must carry a usable `changes` array. Malformed **entries are dropped**, matching every per-field reader in the module (mobs, vehicles, containers, effects, stats) — one bad pair must not cost a player their world — while a malformed **save** (no `seed`, no `players` array, unknown version) still reads as no save at all. Deep per-field validation stays in the restorers (`restoreInventorySlots`, `restoreEffects`, `restoreMobs`, …), which are already total; duplicating it here would give the format two places to disagree about what a player is. Block ids are deliberately **not** allow-listed against `BlockId` — it's a `const enum` with nothing to enumerate at runtime, and a hand-maintained ceiling would silently discard legitimate blocks the first time someone appends an id and forgets to raise it (an unknown id already degrades to magenta via `BLOCK_COLORS[block] ?? [1, 0, 1]`, which is cheaper than data loss).
